newsitem.title: USA: Texas congressmen urge EPA to delay air standards.
newsitem.headline: Texas congressmen urge EPA to delay air standards.

text.p: Most of Texas' congressional delegation, including its two Republican senators, urged the Environmental Protection Agency in a letter released Thursday to delay imposing new air quality standards.

The letter, signed by 26 of the state's 32 congressmen urged EPA Administrator Carol Browner to conduct more research and take more time to study the proposed change in standards for soot and smog pollution.
Texas is on record opposing the EPA's proposal to strengthen air quality standards. The agency is to announce its final decision in July.

The Texas delegation's letter said at least nine additional areas in the state that would be out of compliance with the proposed smog standard, and several counties would not meet the new soot standard.
